Docs quote: 'Asynchronous inserts shift batching responsibility from the client to the server by writing incoming data to an in-memory buffer, then flushing it to storage based on configurable thresholds.' claim: Iceberg tracks individual files, not directories: table metadata file (schema, partitioning, snapshots) -> snapshot -> manifest list (per-manifest partition stats) -> manifest files (one row per data/delete file with partition values and column metrics) -> data files
quote: This table format tracks individual data files in a table instead of directories. ... Table state is maintained in metadata files. All changes to table state create a new metadata file and replace the old metadata with an atomic swap. ... Data files in snapshots are tracked by one or more manifest files ... The manifests that make up a snapshot are stored in a manifest list file.
note: Quoted from format/spec.md on apache/iceberg main (same content as the site).

claim: Optimistic concurrency: writers build new metadata then commit by atomically swapping the table's metadata pointer (in the catalog); if the base snapshot changed they retry; readers never lock
quote: An atomic swap of one table metadata file for another provides the basis for serializable isolation. ... it commits by swapping the table's metadata file pointer from the base version to the new version. If the snapshot on which an update is based is no longer current, the writer must retry the update
note: commit.retry.num-retries default 4 (docs/configuration.md).

claim: Schema evolution by field id: columns are resolved by id, so renames keep the id and add/drop/reorder are safe
quote: Renaming an existing field must change the name, but not the field ID. ... Columns in Iceberg data files are selected by field id. The table schema's column names and order may change after a data file is written, and projection must be done using field ids.

claim: Hidden partitioning: partition values come from transforms of source columns defined in the partition spec, queries filter on data values, and the partition spec can evolve
quote: Partitioning will be table configuration. Reads will be planned using predicates on data values, not partition values. Tables will support evolving partition schemes. ... A transform that is applied to the source column(s) to produce a partition value

claim: Delta commits are JSON files in _delta_log named by version zero-padded to 20 digits; each is atomic and records add/remove actions; writers write data files optimistically then commit by adding the next log entry; vacuum deletes unreferenced files after a retention period (default 7 days)
quote: Delta Log Entries, also known as Delta files, are JSON files stored in the _delta_log directory at the root of the table. ... Delta files are the unit of atomicity for a table, and are named using the next available version number, zero-padded to 20 digits. ... they commit, creating the latest atomic version of the table by adding a new entry to the log. In this log entry they record which data files to logically add and remove ... (default 7 days)
note: Protocol now also defines catalog-managed tables with staged commits in _delta_log/_staged_commits ratified by a catalog.

claim: Checkpoints (Parquet) hold the full replayed table state at a version; Delta Spark writes one every 10 commits by default (delta.checkpointInterval = 10)
quote: A checkpoint contains the complete replay of all actions, up to and including the checkpointed table version, with invalid actions removed. ... "checkpointInterval", "10"
note: The protocol itself says checkpoints 'can be created at any time, for any committed version'; the 10-commit default is the Delta Spark implementation (table property delta.checkpointInterval).

claim: Deletion vectors mark rows deleted in a data file without rewriting it; require reader v3/writer v7 with the deletionVectors table feature
quote: A table's add and remove actions can optionally include a DV that provides information about logically deleted rows, that are however still physically present in the underlying data file and must thus be skipped during processing.

claim: Liquid clustering (CLUSTER BY) replaces partitioning and ZORDER; keys can be changed without rewriting data; incremental via OPTIMIZE; Delta Lake 3.1.0+
quote: Liquid clustering provides flexibility to redefine clustering columns without rewriting existing data ... Liquid clustering is incremental, meaning that data is only rewritten as necessary ... This feature is available in Delta Lake 3.1.0 and above.
